# Verifies whether the frog suspects the truthfulness of the rhino.
# Uses three-valued logic: True, False, or None (unknown). A rule's
# antecedent counts only if it is known, since the question asks for certainty.

def evaluate():
    # Given facts
    badger_money = 88
    frog_money = 72
    frog_friends = 13
    movie_release_year = 1971
    # Lionel Messi was born on 24 June 1987
    messi_birth_year = 1987

    # Unknown predicates start as None
    frog_neglects_swallow = None
    frog_surrenders_poodle = None
    frog_suspects_rhino = None
    frog_surrenders_mule = None  # not stated in the game state

    # Rule2: more money than the badger -> neglects swallow
    if frog_money > badger_money:
        frog_neglects_swallow = True
    # Rule3: movie released before Messi was born -> neglects swallow
    if movie_release_year < messi_birth_year:
        frog_neglects_swallow = True
    # Rule5: more than nine friends -> surrenders to poodle
    if frog_friends > 9:
        frog_surrenders_poodle = True

    print("Rule2 money check:", frog_money, ">", badger_money, "=", frog_money > badger_money)
    print("Rule3 movie check:", movie_release_year, "<", messi_birth_year, "=", movie_release_year < messi_birth_year)
    print("Rule5 friends check:", frog_friends, ">", 9, "=", frog_friends > 9)
    print("frog neglects swallow:", frog_neglects_swallow)
    print("frog surrenders to poodle:", frog_surrenders_poodle)

    # Rule1 (preferred over Rule4) needs CERTAIN "does not surrender to mule"
    rule1_fires = (frog_surrenders_mule is False) and (frog_neglects_swallow is True)
    # Rule4: surrenders to poodle -> suspects rhino
    rule4_fires = (frog_surrenders_poodle is True)

    if rule1_fires:
        frog_suspects_rhino = False
    elif rule4_fires:
        frog_suspects_rhino = True

    print("Rule1 fires (certain):", rule1_fires)
    print("Rule4 fires:", rule4_fires)
    print("frog suspects rhino:", frog_suspects_rhino)

    # Sensitivity: the mule status is unknown, so both substitutions are shown.
    # Only the False case would block Rule4; it is not established by the facts.
    for mule_value in (True, False):
        r1 = (mule_value is False) and (frog_neglects_swallow is True)
        r4 = (frog_surrenders_poodle is True)
        outcome = False if r1 else (True if r4 else None)
        print("if surrenders to mule =", mule_value, "-> suspects rhino =", outcome)

    # Verdict: certainty-only reasoning yields True, so the claim is "Proved"
    verdict = "proved" if frog_suspects_rhino is True else (
        "disproved" if frog_suspects_rhino is False else "unknown")
    print("verdict:", verdict)

    if verdict == "proved" and frog_neglects_swallow is True and frog_surrenders_poodle is True:
        print("CHECK PASS")
    elif verdict == "unknown":
        print("UNSUPPORTED")
        print("CHECK UNKNOWN")
    else:
        print("CHECK FAIL")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    evaluate()
